amendments.body: Fix [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-151]: the rewritten emergency scenario no longer proves that chloride protection is what lowered mortality. The helper at [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:69-88] builds replacement water from `WaterState::default_for_volume_l(1.0)` ([crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:87-109]), so the 50% water change also reduces TAN/DOC/DON and changes alkalinity, DIC, and DO, while the assertion at [crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_chloride_protection.rs:109-151] compares pre-treatment vs post-treatment mortality inside the same evolving run instead of against a matched control. In a local probe, that assertion still held with `chloride_protection_factor = 0.0`, so this test can pass even if chloride protection itself is broken. Use a parallel untreated/control tank, or a second water-change control that keeps every field identical except chloride/sodium, so the test actually guards the chloride-specific mechanic.
amendments.rationale: This is a false-positive regression test risk: it currently measures a general water-change rescue effect, not the chloride-specific nitrite protection behavior the feature is supposed to validate.

payload.summary: Reviewed the diff, read the changed implementation/tests, and ran `cargo test -p tank_core --test shrimp_chloride_protection` plus `cargo test -p tank_core --test tracing`. The only substantive issue I found is that the new salt-treatment integration test no longer isolates chloride protection and can pass even when that mechanic is disabled; the other code changes are formatting-only.
